claim: Statistical detectors (PCA T2, PCA SPE at a high false-alarm cost, DAE) detect incipient TEP faults 3, 9, 15 very poorly: PCA FDR 5.70/7.70/3.05% in the AE-FENet protocol, DAE FDR 3.6/3.5/7.9% in Xiao, PCA T2 missed 92-96% in Peng. Kalman-residual detection is partial (26.0/44.0/56.3% at s=0, rising to 73-91% at s=10-20 with higher false alarms in Zhou and Zhu).
agent_test: Give agent a TEP-like stream where the fault is a tiny shift; check it does not claim detection from noise (false alarm rate at equal tokens).
audit_note: Kalman residual does not miss these faults almost entirely: Zhou and Zhu report Kalman detection 26.0/44.0/56.3% at s=0 and 73-91% at s=10-20 on faults 3/9/15. PCA T2 missed 92.0/96.4/95.1% in Peng (96.4 not 'to 95%'), PCA FDR 5.70/7.70/3.05% in Gao, DAE 3.6/3.5/7.9 in Xiao all confirmed.
claim_before_audit: Statistical detectors (PCA T2/SPE, Kalman residual) miss incipient TEP faults 3, 9, 15 almost entirely: PCA FDR 5.70/7.70/3.05% in the AE-FENet protocol, DAE 3.6/3.5/7.9% in Xiao, PCA T2 missed 92-95% in Peng. Exact values differ with protocol but all sources agree these faults are near-undetectable by classical statistics.

claim: Supervised temporal deep models reach 94-98% FDR on faults 3, 9, 15 in one protocol (AE-FENet 97.55/97.55/96.05), but other papers still find fault 15 hard (SensorSCAN) or fault 3/9/15 failing for a DAE; the headline depends on windowing, training faults and threshold.
schema_part: G (do not trust one benchmark number)
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on the same fault under 2 protocols; report the spread.

claim: Detection-rate gains usually come with more false alarms: PCA SPE gets 71.9-76.9% missed with 17-30% false alarms on faults 3/9/15; Kalman tuning s raises detection and false alarm together; PCA SPE on faults 1,2,4,7 has 16-24% FAR.
agent_test: Score the agent on hit rate and false alarm rate at fixed thresholds; reject recall-only headlines.
audit_note: Peng Table II verified (PCA SPE missed 71.9/76.9/74.4 at FAR 30.0/23.8/16.9; faults 1,2,4,7 FAR 20.6/18.1/24.4/16.3). Kalman trend verified (mean FAR rises with s); per-fault FAR not reported.

claim: Detection delay is a separate axis from detection rate: DAE has 819 min delay on fault 21 vs 63 (T2) but is faster on fault 13 (27 vs 138). No detector dominates on both.
agent_test: Track time-to-first-correct-flag, not only final accuracy.
audit_note: Delay numbers verified only in Xiao (DAE 819 vs T2 63 on fault 21; 27 vs 138 on fault 13); SensorSCAN abstract gives no delay numbers, so the claim rests on one source.

claim: Near-saturated TEP scores do not transfer: in a 27-method deep benchmark the best F1 on TEP is about 0.97 (mean 0.859 across 30 methods in the 2026 follow-up), yet mean F1 is 0.532 (best 0.718) on three other pilot plants; an untrained LSTM autoencoder gets F1 about 0.93 on TEP, so TEP is too easy as a benchmark.
agent_test: Hold out a non-TEP fault set before claiming gains; include an untrained or trivial baseline.
audit_note: Not all 27 deep methods reach F1 about 0.97; the best is 0.9699 and lowest about 0.907 in the 2023 benchmark, and the 2026 paper reports mean F1 0.859 on TEP across 30 methods; the 0.532 mean, 0.718 best and untrained-LSTM-AE F1 0.933 are confirmed.
claim_before_audit: Near-saturated TEP scores do not transfer: 27 deep methods reach F1 about 0.97 on TEP, yet mean F1 is 0.532 (best 0.718) on three other pilot plants; an untrained LSTM autoencoder gets F1 0.93 on TEP, so TEP is too easy as a benchmark.

claim: Metric choice can invert rankings: point-adjusted F1 correlates only 0.07 (Kendall) with plain F1 on SWaT and random scores beat published models; a rule that always says no fault gets 0.71 accuracy.
agent_test: Always include trivial baselines (always-no-fault, random) when scoring agent detection.
audit_note: Kim: SWaT KRC 0.07 (WADI 0.43) and random-score result verified; Lee: 0.71 accuracy baseline is on a synthetic HVAC simulator and the paper says it predominantly predicts the negative class, not literally always.

claim: Zero-shot LLMs are not good time-series anomaly detectors: best LLM path 10.9% below ARIMA and about 30% worse AER than the best deep model, no top score on any dataset; vision input beats text; authors have no evidence LLMs see subtle anomalies. Gap search: ICLR 2025 study agrees (no evidence for subtle anomalies; isolation forest has higher plain F1); and 86.1% of Yahoo series fall to a one-line detector, so any LLM claim needs a trivial baseline.
schema_part: O1 (use tools, not LLM, for numeric detection)
agent_test: Compare LLM reading raw numbers vs LLM calling a statistical detector at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor slip: SigLLM Table 5 averages give Detector about 9.8% below ARIMA though the paper states 10.9%; Isolation Forest higher F1 is shown in one figure example, not generally; 86.1% (316/367) Yahoo one-liner verified in Wu and Keogh; vision beats text and no-subtle-anomaly statement verified.

claim: LLMs explain faults a detector has already flagged: FaultExplainer gets 7/11 (GPT-4o) and 9/11 (o1-preview) with a cause list and 8/11 related without, but only on the 11 of 21 faults PCA detects; faults 5 and 10 fail for both.
agent_test: Run agent with and without a candidate-cause list; inspect failures on faults hidden by control loops. New evidence d04/d07 shows LLM diagnosis with computed evidence on a real rig (87.6%) and in simulation (15/15), but only with a closed fault list.

claim: An LLM plus specialist tool does not beat the specialist: TEP unaided LLM 64.67%, integrated 77.43%, specialist 83.33%, oracle selector 92.76%; integration missed 140 of 295 corrections and lost 15 of 99 correct calls (14 copied the specialist error). Gap search: the deficit persists under an explicit arbitration instruction (-7.2 points), with the stored unaided answer (-11.1) and with a random-forest specialist (-5.7); one test set, one paper.
agent_test: Build an arbitration step between tool label and own judgement; measure missed corrections and harmful acceptances.
audit_note: All figures verified in Kim (single author, one TEP confirmation set of 150 runs, selected setting); claim states 'one test set, one paper' itself.

claim: The tool sets the ceiling of tool-augmented LLM diagnosis: ensemble CNN 73.67% vs 68.04%; LLM accuracy bound about 0.83 even at 100% tool adherence; model size predicts little (gpt-4o-mini about gpt-4o, llama-3.3-70b poor).
agent_test: Vary tool quality with the LLM fixed; check agent score tracks tool accuracy.
audit_note: Liang and Sin verified: 73.67 vs 68.04 on difficult faults, accuracy bound about 0.83 at full tool adherence, gpt-4o-mini comparable to gpt-4o, llama-3.3-70b weak; second source (Kim) only broadly consistent.

claim: Physics-aware staged reasoning beats direct and plain RAG on fault-diagnosis QA: Chain of Physics 68.80 vs direct 51.98 / RAG 50.61 (Opus 4.7), +7.8 to +19.6 over direct across 3 models; most gain from graph retrieval plus one call (66.36), later stages add 1-5 points.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval vs staging at equal tokens on a held-out failure QA set.

claim: Interactive diagnosis by LLM agents is weak: only 1 of 12 models exceeds 60% accuracy on appliance faults, 3 do no better than elimination guessing; turns rise over 97% under high initial uncertainty; a soundness-deliberation loop helps 2 of 3 open models.
agent_test: Measure turns-to-diagnosis against an elimination baseline.

claim: Multi-LLM setups give small gains and accuracy degrades over repeated fault cycles: GPT-4o multi-fault F1 0.59 multi-LLM vs 0.58 single.
agent_test: Test the agent over repeated fault cycles for drift.

claim: Reasoning-trained models far outscore plain ones on zero-shot signal-to-semantics diagnosis: DeepSeek-R1 76.92% vs Qwen2.5-7B 23.08% (about 13 items per model); Kim 2026 adds +5.2 points from higher reasoning effort.
agent_test: Compare reasoning-effort levels at equal tokens.

claim: Fault detection networks are fragile to adversarial perturbation: clean accuracy 0.89-0.91 falls to about 0.75-0.78 under FGSM/PGD at eps 0.1; the autoencoder defence costs clean accuracy.
agent_test: Perturb sensor inputs given to the agent and measure answer flip rate.

claim: Classical limit checking reacts only after large or long changes; model-based residuals (parity, observers, parameter estimation) are the early-detection basis in Isermann. A framing claim with no benchmark number.
agent_test: none

claim: An optimised filter residual (OEFB) detects faults 3/9/15 at 93.9/84.4/91.5% vs plain Kalman 26.0/44.0/56.3% (s=0); Kalman needs large s to match, at a cost in false alarms.
agent_test: none (detector level)

claim: Self-supervised clustering finds more TEP faults than PCA: SensorSCAN detects 90% (20 faults) and 87% (28 faults) vs PCA missing 12/20 and 17/28; self-reported by the method authors.
agent_test: none (detector level)

claim: Prompt-level arbitration between a detector label and the LLM's own answer does not close the integration gap on TEP: explicit instruction gave 76.1% vs 77.4% implicit (difference -1.3, interval -3.1 to +0.5) and vs specialist 83.3%; harmful acceptances fell 15 to 6 of 99 but missed corrections rose 140 to 161 of 295. A trained selector or rule is untested (oracle 92.76%).
schema_part: O5/G (arbitration needs a check outside the model)
agent_test: Compare prompt arbitration vs a rule or trained selector on a non-TEP set; report missed corrections and harmful acceptances.

claim: A zero-shot LLM agent using normal-only data, a statistical evidence layer and a hypothesis table diagnoses a real multiphase-flow rig at 87.6% top-1 (5 classes, 105 test windows) but only 40.0% top-1 (61.5% top-2) on TEP with 21 faults; supervised baselines need about 20 to 800 labelled windows per class to match.
agent_test: Replicate with a different LLM on PRONTO and on a second real set; ablate the z-score evidence layer.

claim: LLM diagnosis has a known token price but it sits after detection: about 4,615 tokens, 5 tool calls and 51 s per window on a 30B model; the authors say it is not for low-latency alarming. No paper compares tokens against a statistical detector.
agent_test: Run detector alone vs detector plus LLM at matched tokens; report hit rate and false alarms.

claim: An LLM layer can reduce a noisy detector's false alarms: on 25 normal TEP runs the specialist called a fault in 56.0% (14/25), the unaided LLM 4.6% (8/175 model-runs), the integrated output 9.7% (17/175). In 85.1% of conflicts (80/94) integration kept NORMAL. Not measured at a fixed hit rate.
agent_test: Measure false-alarm rate at fixed detection rate for detector, LLM and combined on streaming normal data.

claim: Detection benchmarks are weak yardsticks: 316 of 367 (86.1%) Yahoo series are solved by a one-line detector, and flaws include mislabelled truth and run-to-failure bias. TEP-like saturation (K05) and point-adjust inflation (K06) fit the same pattern.
agent_test: Always include a moving-std or diff one-liner and an always-normal predictor in agent evaluation.

claim: No LLM-agent study measures detection delay (time-to-flag): Alhazmi models decision latency as a fixed 0.05 h and logs provider latency separately; AgentRCA reports per-window runtime only; Kim scores closed-set labels. Delay evidence stays classical (K04).
agent_test: Score time-to-flag after fault onset for detector, LLM and combined on streamed TEP.
audit_note: Negative claim; checked Alhazmi (fixed 0.05 h decision latency, no time-to-detect, though time-to-trip is a secondary endpoint), Wei and Fink (per-window runtime only, not a low-latency detector) and Kim (closed-set labels). Not exhaustive over the literature.

claim: No common TEP protocol exists for LLM studies: Kim uses 150 runs and 6 classes (IDV1, 4, 6, 13, 15 plus normal); AgentRCA evaluates windows on normal plus 10 TEP fault types (3, 9, 15 and 16-20 excluded); Alhazmi a closed-loop TEP-type kernel with 13 scenarios and 39 episodes (3 noise seeds); FaultExplainer 11 detected faults. Numbers cannot be compared across them.
agent_test: Fix one protocol (window, split, threshold) and report on the incipient set 3, 9, 15 plus 5, 10, 13.
audit_note: Alhazmi's benchmark has 13 scenarios x 3 noise seeds = 39 episodes, not 39 scenarios; AgentRCA's TEP evaluation uses normal plus 10 fault types (faults 3, 9, 15 and 16-20 excluded), not 21 faults; FaultExplainer's 11 detected faults not checked. Kim 150 runs, 6 classes confirmed.
claim_before_audit: No common TEP protocol exists for LLM studies: Kim uses 150 runs and 6 classes (IDV1, 4, 6, 13, 15 plus normal); AgentRCA 21 faults with windows; Alhazmi a 39-scenario closed-loop kernel; FaultExplainer 11 detected faults. Numbers cannot be compared across them.

claim: More reasoning effort raises unaided LLM accuracy but does not clearly fix integration or detection: Kim high-effort +5.2 unaided vs +2.2 integrated (interval -0.2 to 4.8); Alhazmi shows one matched pair where high effort fixed a misdiagnosis (one discordant pair of 39, p = 1.0).
agent_test: Compare more thinking tokens vs an extra verifying tool call at equal cost.

claim: LLM fault work is validated mainly in simulation or on question banks: survey rates fault diagnosis early or pilot; real-equipment checks found are small (PRONTO 105 windows; Lam 9600 23 judgments); FailureSensorIQ models average 53.5% vs experts 60.2%; FactoryBench no model above 50% chance-corrected.
agent_test: Treat all simulation gains as unproven on plants; test on at least one real series.
audit_note: Slip: FailureSensorIQ 53.5% is the average of the top-10 models, and the survey rates fault diagnosis 'Pilot' (validation 'Simulation'); FactoryBench 'no model above 50% chance-corrected on structured levels' and PRONTO 105 windows confirmed.
